newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht, interbank rate steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht, interbank rate steady in late trade.

text.p: The baht was steady against the dollar in late trade on Wednesday despite the U.S. unit's sharp fall abroad, dealers said.

"The dollar did not weaken much against the baht although the U.S. unit dipped against major currencies. Some domestic banks heavily bought the dollar in the afternoon to cover their position," one dealer at a European bank said.
The baht was steady at 25.927/25.930 to the dollar late compared with 25.927/25.932 in early morning, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.92 per dollar against 25.96 on Tuesday.
The overnight interbank rate was unchanged at 9.50-10.00 percent late and dealers expected continued demand for funds over the rest of this week, dealers said.
"The demand will remain strong this week on the upcoming reserve requirement and long weekend," said one money market dealer.
All commercial banks have to meet the Bank of Thailand's reserve requirement on the seventh and 22nd of each month. Next Monday is a public holiday.
The central bank's policy of keeping interbank rates high would also stem any sharp fall in rates, dealers said.
Central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Wednesday he favoured high interbank rates to attract capital inflow. He said an overnight interbank rate of five to seven percent was too low.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was quoted at 7.00/8.00 satangs per dollar late compared with 7.50/8.50 in the morning.
